title: TLS certificate hostname bypass when the host loosely resolves to an IP address
vulnerabilityInformation: A flaw was discovered in TLS hostname verification that could allow a server certificate to be validated against a different IP address than the one the client connected to. This occurred when a host used a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, as the certificate validation normalization followed different rules than the operating system resolver on some platforms. The vulnerability affected multiple versions of Node.js.
